newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Golf-Els defies monsoon weather to open two-shot lead.
newsitem.headline: Golf-Els defies monsoon weather to open two-shot lead.

text.p: World number three Ernie Els of South Africa took wet fairways and monsoon weather in his stride on Friday to shoot a one-under-par 71 and open a two-stroke lead in the eight-player, country-hopping Johnnie Walker Super Tour.
Els recovered from a bad start to shoot three birdies on the back nine for a 71 and a three-round total of seven-under-par 209.
After rounds in Taipei, Seoul and here at the Orchard Golf and Country Club, the four-city tournament flies into Bangkok on Sunday for the final round.
Els, the former U.S. Open champion, leads from Scotland's Colin Montgomerie, who also handled the conditions well to card a 71, and Ian Woosnam. The Welshman shot a one-over-par 73.
Montgomerie said: "The key for me today was that I drove the ball better...I am getting tired physically and mentally but the other players are as well."
The par-72, 7,013-yard layout was sodden from heavy rains during the ironically named Typhoon Ernie. Woosnam quipped: "If it had been any worse we would have been playing with snorkels."

The third leg of the tournament was launched by keen golfer President Fidel Ramos of the Philippines who hit a tee shot straight and far down the first fairway to a huge cheer from the gallery of a 1,000 people.
